paragraphs.zh: It is another object of the present disclosure to provide an economical, efficient and eco-friendly process for preparation of mesotrione.
paragraphs.en: It is another object of the present disclosure to provide an economical, efficient and eco-friendly process for preparation of mesotrione.
paragraphs.notes: First paragraph on the page and it begins a complete sentence, so nothing is carried over from p05. Marker printed as exactly four digits on the page. Printed over two lines and joined with a single space per brief rule 3. No left margin line number sits beside this paragraph.
Bold section heading, left aligned, no paragraph marker. It governs everything that follows on this page, which is why both drawings below are read as the invention's own route.

paragraphs.zh: The foregoing and other objects are attained by the present disclosure, which in one aspect provides a process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst.
paragraphs.en: The foregoing and other objects are attained by the present disclosure, which in one aspect provides a process for preparation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) by oxidation of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst.
paragraphs.notes: Both spellings of the same moiety appear in this one sentence and are kept exactly as printed: 'methylsulphonyl' with a PH for the benzoic acid, 'methylsulfonyl' with an F for the toluene, three lines apart. This is the OPPOSITE assignment from the brief section 8 table, which pairs sulphonyl with NMST and sulfonyl with NMSBA. What the page prints is what is transcribed. This paragraph is where the formula numbers attach to the abbreviations: NMSBA = formula (III), NMST = formula (IV). RuO2 is printed with a subscript 2, flattened here to a plain 2. Left margin line number 5 sits beside the first line and is furniture, excluded. Marker printed as exactly four digits.

paragraphs.zh: In another aspect, there is provided a process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione. The method disclosed herein is extremely advantageous over the methods existing in the art for the preparation of enol ester, in that it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC).
paragraphs.en: In another aspect, there is provided a process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1,3-cyclohexanedione. The method disclosed herein is extremely advantageous over the methods existing in the art for the preparation of enol ester, in that it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC).
paragraphs.notes: Both occurrences here are spelled 'methylsulphonyl' with a PH, for NMSBA and for NMSBC alike; unlike the preceding paragraph this one is internally consistent. This is the second place where a formula number attaches to an abbreviation: the enol ester = formula (II), NMSBA = formula (III) again. NMSBC is named in prose only and is NOT drawn anywhere on this page. Printed over six lines and joined with single spaces. Left margin line numbers 10 and 15 sit beside the first and last lines and are furniture, excluded. Marker printed as exactly four digits.

It ends on a colon that introduces an enumerated list of steps, and that list is not on this page: it continues on p07. Nothing is invented to complete it. This paragraph names mesotrione as formula (I), the third and last formula number bound on this page, but formula (I) is not drawn here. Marker printed as exactly four digits. No left margin line number beside it.

drawings.notes: Label to structure pairing, checked at 3x and then 8x on the label row alone: 'Formula IV' sits under the LEFT structure, the one bearing CH3, and 'Formula III' sits under the RIGHT structure, the one bearing COOH. The label row carries exactly two inked groups and no third, so neither structure is unlabelled and nothing is labelled that is not a structure. The pairing agrees with the prose of the paragraph immediately above, which calls the toluene formula (IV) and the benzoic acid formula (III). presented_as is invention_route, judged from the page and not assumed: the heading directly above is SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION and the sentence that introduces the scheme reads 'attained by the present disclosure, which in one aspect provides a process', so the page presents this step as the disclosure's own. Nothing here is attributed to the art. The arrow is one continuous horizontal line with a single solid filled arrowhead at its right end; the ink is degraded and pixelated but not broken into segments, so the style is solid. The text 'Oxidant / RuO2' is written ABOVE the arrow, left of centre; nothing at all is written BELOW the arrow. The 2 of RuO2 is a subscript, flattened here. The nitro groups are printed as the label NO2 with no formal charges; the charge-separated [N+](=O)[O-] in the SMILES is a notation convention, not something drawn. Ring positions were counted off the drawn hexagon vertices in both structures, not inferred from the names in the prose.

drawings.notes: Label to structure pairing, checked at 8x on the label row alone: 'Formula III' sits under the LEFT structure, the benzoic acid, and 'Formula II' sits under the RIGHT structure, the enol ester. The label row of this scheme carries exactly two inked groups, at x 357-455 and x 1141-1232; the middle structure spans roughly x 520-830 and has nothing printed under it, so the 1,3-cyclohexanedione is genuinely unlabelled and neither formula number belongs to it. 'Formula III' therefore labels the same compound in both schemes on this page, and the two drawings of it agree substituent for substituent. Distinguishing 'Formula III' from 'Formula II' was done by counting the strokes of the numeral at 8x, three against two, since at page scale the degraded ink makes them look alike. presented_as is invention_route, judged from the page: the paragraph immediately above says 'there is provided a process', and the same paragraph contrasts this route with 'the methods existing in the art', which places the drawn route on the disclosure's side of that contrast rather than in the art. The arrow carries NOTHING above it and NOTHING below it: no reagent, no solvent, no temperature, no catalyst. Its ink is broken into a regular row of dots at page scale, but every bond in the two structures either side of it is broken in exactly the same way in this scan, the arrowhead is a single solid filled triangle, and the brief section 9 records the same degradation on p15, so this is recorded as a solid line and not a dashed one. Arrow confidence is medium for that reason alone; the structures either side are high. Ring positions in all three structures were counted off the drawn vertices. In the enol ester the C1=C2 double bond and the C3 ketone were confirmed on a separate 5x crop of the alicyclic ring, so the 3-oxocyclohex-1-en-1-yl connectivity is read off the drawing, not deduced from what a cyclohexane-1,3-dione ester 'should' look like. The nitro group is again printed as the label NO2 with no formal charges.

discrepancies.what: The scheme in paragraph 15 writes oxidant and catalyst as one slash-separated string above the arrow and does not name the oxidant, while the prose distinguishes the two roles and names the catalyst.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Oxidant / RuO2, written above the arrow as a single label, with nothing below the arrow; the oxidant itself is not named and the label does not say which of the two is the catalyst.
discrepancies.text_says: 'using an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst', which names RuO2 explicitly as the catalyst and leaves the oxidant unnamed as well.

discrepancies.what: The page spells the same methylsulfonyl moiety two ways within a single sentence of paragraph 15, while the drawings carry no spelling at all and so cannot settle it.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Nothing. The structures are drawn with SO2 and H3C labels only, and the printed captions are the formula numbers Formula IV, Formula III and Formula II, which carry no compound name.
discrepancies.text_says: '2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA)' with a PH and '2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST)' with an F, three lines apart in the same sentence. Paragraph 16 then uses the PH form for both NMSBA and NMSBC. Both are transcribed as printed and neither is normalised.

discrepancies.what: The prose of paragraph 16 names an intermediate that the scheme beside it does not draw.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Two reactants and one product only: the benzoic acid, 1,3-cyclohexanedione, and the enol ester. No acid chloride appears anywhere in the drawing.
discrepancies.text_says: 'it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC)'. The absence from the drawing is consistent with the claim being made, and is recorded here only so that a later pass does not read NMSBC as a drawn species on this page.
